text:
amy_support: Heads-up — AcmeApp flagged that after the v4.3 rollout their downstream JSON parsers are failing. They say fields that used to be arrays are coming back as null.

sophie_cs: Pasted customer error: "Failed to parse payload: expected array for 'items' but got null at /response/items". They sent an example payload and said it worked yesterday. :grimacing:

devon_oncall: @amy_support can you attach the request id + model_version from the failing call? Also did this come in during the canary cutover window?

amy_support: Request id: r-0a9c71bf, model returned header: model: redwood-llm-4.3-opt. Timestamp matches deploy-bot event below. Customer reports this started immediately after 02:08Z.

deploy-bot: canary deploy finished: redwood-llm-4.3-opt -> canary group, commit abc123, at 2026-03-17T02:07:52Z.

luca_ml: Quick hypothesis — tokenizer or output post-process changed behavior for empty sequences. Could be a change in the streaming JSON buffer policy that collapses empty arrays to nulls when KV cache is present.

marta_eng: Can you paste a minimal repro? If we can reproduce locally we can narrow to runtime vs model artifact.

sophie_cs: Customer sent minimal curl: 

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-customer" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-llm-4.3-opt","mode":"json","prompt":"Return JSON {\"items\": []}"}'

Response body they got: 
{
  "response": {
    "items": null,
    "meta": {"processing_time_ms": 123}
  }
}

They say calling same request with model redwood-llm-4.2-compat returns items: [] as expected.

devon_oncall: Repro steps for us: 1) run that curl with a staging token against canary pool 2) check serving runtime logs for request r-0a9c71bf 3) grep for any post-processing path that touches structured output.

luca_ml: Also check either tokenizer config or any ``auto_coerce_empty_sequences`` flag. I pushed a quick diff to my branch earlier that changed how empty sequence tokens are emitted during quantized sampling; maybe that landed in 4.3.

amy_support: Customer also noticed a token usage spike — they saw ~4x token counts for a template that was stable. They flagged billing team but want immediate fix.

marta_eng: Noted. If it's a behavioral change in model outputs we should treat as regressive and rollback the canary. But if it's a runtime post-process bug we can hotfix.

deploy-bot: rollout status: 4.3-opt canary at 60% traffic since 02:12Z, 100% scheduled at 02:30Z unless blocked.

devon_oncall: Blocking the 100% promotion now. I'm pausing the rollout and initiating an immediate rollback to 4.2-compat for affected customer segment. Oncall ticket: #INC-5421.

luca_ml: I'll run a quick compare between model logits/dump for a test prompt on 4.2-compat vs 4.3-opt. If the model is emitting a different sentinel token for empty sequences, that's a behavioral model change.

amy_support: I asked customer for the full request+response headers and they uploaded logs to the ticket.

sophie_cs: Customer asked for workaround — suggested pinning model to redwood-llm-4.2-compat or adding a local check to coerce null -> [] for the field "items". They prefer a server-side fix.

marta_eng: Action items: 
- devon_oncall: keep canary paused and rollback if more customers show failures (assigned)
- luca_ml: diff model artifacts and tokenization between 4.2 and 4.3 (assigned)
- marta_eng: add a short-term runtime guard to preserve empty arrays during structured output streaming path (assigned)
- amy_support/sophie_cs: collect customer sample corpus and repros, update ticket and notify billing about token spike scope (assigned)

amy_support: Customer calm for now; asked for ETA. I told them were investigating and might rollback cluster-level changes in the next 60–90m.

luca_ml: Found preliminary artifact diff: a small change in output conditioning that can emit a special "<EMPTY_LIST>" sentinel which the post-processor was supposed to convert to [] but the conversion path wasn't executed under continuous-batching. Looks like the conversion code was refactored in 4.3.

marta_eng: Good find. If conversion didn't run under continuous-batching that's a runtime bug not a model semantics change. That points to a hotfix path.

devon_oncall: Rolling a hotfix to the streaming post-process now to ensure sentinel -> [] conversion is executed even when early chunking happens. Will push a canary patch to the canary pool and re-run customer repro.

(10 minutes later)

deploy-bot: canary patch deployed: streaming-fix-4.3.1 -> canary group at 2026-03-17T02:35:10Z.

luca_ml: Re-ran the customer curl against patched canary and got:

{
  "response": {
    "items": [],
    "meta": {"processing_time_ms": 130}
  }
}

amy_support: Customer confirmed the patched canary returns arrays now and parser error cleared. They asked us to keep them pinned to the patched region for 24h while they run batch jobs.

marta_eng: Plan: promote patch to prod after 2h of canary validation and close incident if no new regressions. Follow-up: open an RFC to add structured-output integration tests across batching/streaming modes to prevent this.

amy_support: Ticket updated with root cause -> missing conversion call in streaming path. Customer happy with workaround. Closing loop with billing team re: token spike — looks like spike correlates with conversion failure causing longer fallback text sequences, will need small credit.

sophie_cs: I'll draft a short postmortem for CS to send to AcmeApp.

marta_eng: Thanks everyone. Dropping a follow-on issue to add an invariant test.

(incident closed: INC-5421 - temporary patch -> promoted, monitor)
